craft_claim: Manufactured urgency is defined by fabricated deadlines or scarcity, inflated or unverifiable consequences, and pressure with no real action; it is detectable by asking whether the deadline resets and whether the stated cost is verifiable.

supporting_evidence.note: Scarcity is catalogued as a persuasion lever, which is exactly why its use must be tethered to a real constraint; the lever works whether or not the scarcity is genuine.

supporting_evidence.location: Psychology & Marketing 8(1), pp. 43-57 (scarcity effects on value)
supporting_evidence.note: The meta-analytic review supports the claim that perceived scarcity raises value; this establishes the mechanism that fake scarcity exploits, and therefore the ethical line the repository draws.
Because scarcity narrows judgment, fabricated scarcity is not a neutral stylistic choice; it degrades the reader's ability to evaluate the claim.

counterevidence.location: The Myth of the Rhetorical Situation, pp. 154-161
counterevidence.note: Vatz's constructivism can be read as licensing the rhetor to create salience. The repository's rule rejects that license for urgency: constructed salience without a real exigence is the failure case, not the method.

scope: All forms, and especially marketing/copy where scarcity and countdowns are conventionally used.
exceptions: A real, verifiable constraint may be stated as scarcity.
Fiction and satire may stage manufactured urgency visibly, with the staging as the point.
